data.label: Receive Order
data.description: Accept an inbound customer order and emit the initial workflow event with idempotency and telemetry.

data.label: Validate Payload
data.description: Check the order schema and required fields before downstream processing.

data.label: Authenticate Customer
data.description: Verify the customer identity and session context for the order.

data.label: Assess Fraud Risk
data.description: Evaluate fraud score and route high-risk or high-value orders to human review.

data.label: Verify Payment Method
data.description: Confirm a usable payment method is on file and eligible for capture.

data.label: Reserve Inventory
data.description: Reserve stock for each line item against available inventory.

data.label: Split by Fulfillment Center
data.description: Partition the order into shipments or packages by fulfillment center.

data.label: Price Order
data.description: Compute shipping, discounts, loyalty rewards, taxes, and invoice totals.

data.label: Charge Payment
data.description: Attempt to capture payment for the finalized invoice amount.

data.label: Handle Payment Decline
data.description: Retry bounded payment attempts and escalate if payment remains declined.

data.label: Send Order Confirmation
data.description: Notify the customer via email and SMS that the order is confirmed.

data.label: Create Fulfillment Work Order
data.description: Open the fulfillment work order for warehouse execution.

data.label: Pick Pack and Label
data.description: Pick items, pack them in appropriate boxes, and generate shipping labels.

data.label: Schedule and Handoff Shipment
data.description: Schedule carrier pickup, hand off parcels, and begin shipment tracking.

data.label: Track Delivery
data.description: Monitor shipment progress, delivery exceptions, and delay notifications until receipt.

data.label: Confirm Delivery
data.description: Confirm delivery on receipt and request customer review when needed.

data.label: Settle Finance
data.description: Record ledger entries, reconcile captured amounts, and post revenue to accounting.

data.label: Update Analytics
data.description: Refresh sales, inventory, and restock forecasting metrics for reporting.

data.label: Process Returns
data.description: Manage return requests, authorizations, labels, receipt, inspection, restock, disposal, and refund issuance.

data.label: Close and Archive Order
data.description: Finalize the order lifecycle, archive records, and persist audit-ready history.

data.label: Surface Anomalies
data.description: Continuously surface operational anomalies, SLA breaches, and exception alerts to operations.

data.label: Generate Daily Summary
data.description: Produce management reporting and executive summaries from operational and analytics data.

message: The workflow starts with order intake and validation, then proceeds through customer authentication, fraud screening, payment verification, inventory reservation, fulfillment splitting, pricing, and payment capture. Successful orders fan out into confirmation, warehouse execution, shipping, delivery tracking, finance settlement, analytics updates, and potential returns handling before closure and archival. Monitoring and reporting run in parallel across the lifecycle, with conditional branches for fraud rejection, payment decline retries, and delivery/returns outcomes.

workflow.workflowBrief:
We operate a high-volume e-commerce order fulfillment platform. Below is an exhaustive description of the end-to-end workflow that must run for every inbound order from submission through final archival. The process must handle happy path flows, payment declines, fraud flags, partial fulfillment, returns, chargebacks, and analytics reporting, with comprehensive logging, monitoring, human review gates for high-value transactions, and strict SLAs on each downstream integration point. Step 1: receive incoming customer order. This step is critical because it interacts with multiple downstream systems, must be idempotent, and must log full diagnostic telemetry for auditing. It may succeed, fail, or produce partial results that require manual review. Retries should be bounded and backed off, and failures should escalate to the operations team when necessary. Appropriate notifications must fire to the customer, the operations team, and internal analytics whenever state changes. Data must be persisted to long-term storage and indexed for reporting. Compliance, privacy, and security constraints must be enforced at every boundary.
